findings.issue_text: Malformed/unschemed website strings silently produce nil for website_name in user_serializer.rb (~137-150), suppressing the website display entirely without any error, due to rescue nil masking parse failures

Inconsistent same-site detection logic in user_serializer.rb (~140): three branches use different notions of 'same domain', and the reverse suffix direction fails (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance example.com shows no path), with an arbitrary label-count heuristic treating unrelated sibling hosts like sub.co.uk vs other.co.uk as 'same site'

Repeated URI(website.to_s) calls without rescue in branches of user_serializer.rb (~142,145,148) are fragile: future edits or different host computation could make unprotected .path calls raise inside a serializer, causing a 500 on the user profile/card endpoint; parse result should be computed once

websiteName computed property removed from user.js.es6 controller with only templates/user/user.hbs updated; other templates or code (e.g. user card) referencing websiteName would render empty — needs a repo-wide grep before merge

Websites without a scheme produce no website_name, silently hiding the link: URI('example.com').host is nil because Ruby's URI parser requires a scheme; include_website_name? returns true but website_name is nil, and the template gates the link on {{#if model.website_name}}, so unparseable saved websites make the profile link vanish entirely instead of showing a degraded fallback
rescue nil swallows URI::InvalidURIError for genuinely malformed input, hitting the same vanishing-link path; a fallback like return website_host || website would prevent the regression

Same-domain display drops the query string and fragment: display string is host + URI(website).path, discarding query and fragment, so http://example.com/page?id=42 is displayed as example.com/page, misleading and inconsistent with the title attribute showing the full URL

Repeated URI(website.to_s) parsing and comparison against discourse_host is done three times per serialization; needless per-row cost in a hot serialization path, and a later parse in the same method isn't covered by the earlier rescue

Malformed/invalid website URL inputs (e.g. 'not a url', 'javascript:alert(1)', '/path') are untested; the second URI(website.to_s).path call on line ~143 is not inside the rescue, so website_host can be nil while include_website_name is still true, emitting website_name: nil unasserted

Second URI() call on line 143/146 without rescue: a value that parses for .host but raises on the second parse, or path edge cases (empty path, trailing slash, 'http://example.com?x=1'), are unverified

Missing test coverage for the sibling-subdomain elsif branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com), including its negative case (www.other.com vs forum.example.com) and off-by-one/subdomain logic risks

No test asserting website_name equals just the host (no path appended) for a length-matching but different domain, nor for empty/trailing-slash paths, nor for query strings being silently dropped by URI#path
Frontend removal of websiteName computed property and switch to model.website_name in templates has zero JS/qunit test coverage; other references to websiteName would silently render empty

Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname with Mocha legacy stubs, coupling tests to the mock; if the implementation caches the hostname at boot the tests still pass while production differs, and there's no integration test that the serializer includes website_name via a real controller response
No test asserts website_name is absent from the JSON when the user has no website; the include_website_name inclusion gate is completely untested, a classic silent-failure point

Removal of `websiteName` computed property from user.js.es6 may break other consumers (mobile templates, user card, plugins/themes) that still reference `websiteName`, causing silent empty rendering; no grep performed to verify remaining references
Serializer builds display path via `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, dropping query strings and fragments, e.g. `http://example.com/search?q=1234` displays as `example.com/search`
Bare `http://example.com/` displays inconsistently as `example.com/` with trailing slash versus `example.com` for scheme-less input

`rescue nil` in `website_name` swallows unparseable website values: `include_website_name` is true when `website.present?` but `website_name` returns nil for values URI() can't parse (e.g. `example.com/user`), causing a present website to silently disappear from the profile; the guard should test the parsed host instead of `website.present?`

Equal-length subdomain heuristic shows full path for unrelated sibling subdomains (e.g. `secret.example.com/private/admin` on host `forum.example.com`), causing inconsistent path-disclosure exposure across users on the same registrable domain

Missing test for the negative case of website-is-subdomain-of-instance (e.g. `sub.example.com` vs `forums.example.com` showing host-only) and for website-present-but-unparseable case, leaving fragile else-branches untested

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed/unschemed website strings silently produce nil for website_name in user_serializer.rb (~137-150), suppressing the website display entirely without any error, due to rescue nil masking parse failures

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return `nil` for inputs URI can’t parse into a host (e.g., unschemed strings like `example.com/user`, or otherwise malformed URIs). The method then `return`s when `website_host.nil?`, and the template only renders the website block when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present-but-unparseable `website` will result in the website not being displayed with no fallback. Whether that’s a defect depends on upstream validation/allowed formats (not shown in the diff), but the diff does introduce this silent “drop” behavior via `rescue nil` and lack of fallback to `website`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent same-site detection logic in user_serializer.rb (~140): three branches use different notions of 'same domain', and the reverse suffix direction fails (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance example.com shows no path), with an arbitrary label-count heuristic treating unrelated sibling hosts like sub.co.uk vs other.co.uk as 'same site'

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` uses multiple inconsistent heuristics for “same-site”/related-domain detection. In the `elsif` branch it treats hosts with the same label-count (>2) as related by comparing `split('.')[1..-1]`, which would incorrectly classify sibling hosts like `sub.co.uk` and `other.co.uk` as related (both reduce to `co.uk`) and then append the path. In the final `else` branch it only checks `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, so the reverse case (website is a subdomain of instance, e.g. `www.example.com` vs instance `example.com`) will not be considered related and will omit the path, matching the finding’s example behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated URI(website.to_s) calls without rescue in branches of user_serializer.rb (~142,145,148) are fragile: future edits or different host computation could make unprotected .path calls raise inside a serializer, causing a 500 on the user profile/card endpoint; parse result should be computed once

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return early if parsing fails (host nil). If parsing succeeds once, re-parsing the same `website.to_s` for `.path` in the branches (`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`) is not shown to be able to raise in the current diff. The finding’s 500-risk claim is speculative (“future edits”) rather than a verifiable issue introduced by this change; at most it’s a minor refactor/perf suggestion to compute `uri = URI(...)` once.

adjudication_records.issue_text: websiteName computed property removed from user.js.es6 controller with only templates/user/user.hbs updated; other templates or code (e.g. user card) referencing websiteName would render empty — needs a repo-wide grep before merge

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name` instead, with `website_name` now provided by `UserSerializer`. The finding claims other templates/components (e.g., user card) still reference `websiteName`, but no such references are shown in the diff, so this cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Websites without a scheme produce no website_name, silently hiding the link: URI('example.com').host is nil because Ruby's URI parser requires a scheme; include_website_name? returns true but website_name is nil, and the template gates the link on {{#if model.website_name}}, so unparseable saved websites make the profile link vanish entirely instead of showing a degraded fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the host is derived via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`; for a saved website like `"example.com"` (no scheme), Ruby’s `URI()` returns a nil `host`, so `website_name` becomes nil. However `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, and the template now renders the website link only under `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so an un-schemed but present website would result in the website link disappearing entirely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: rescue nil swallows URI::InvalidURIError for genuinely malformed input, hitting the same vanishing-link path; a fallback like return website_host || website would prevent the regression

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will set `website_host` to nil for malformed/non-parseable `website` values, then `return if website_host.nil?` causes `website_name` to be nil. The template was changed to render the website section only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present `website` with an invalid URI will now result in the website link disappearing entirely. This is a behavior regression directly caused by the new `rescue nil` + early return path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same-domain display drops the query string and fragment: display string is host + URI(website).path, discarding query and fragment, so http://example.com/page?id=42 is displayed as example.com/page, misleading and inconsistent with the title attribute showing the full URL

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the display string is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in multiple branches (e.g. same-domain case), which by definition omits `URI(...).query` and `URI(...).fragment`. Therefore a URL like `http://example.com/page?id=42#x` would produce `website_name` of `example.com/page`, while the template still uses the full `model.website` for `href` and `title`, creating an inconsistent/misleading display introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated URI(website.to_s) parsing and comparison against discourse_host is done three times per serialization; needless per-row cost in a hot serialization path, and a later parse in the same method isn't covered by the earlier rescue

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the same string is parsed multiple times (`URI(website.to_s)` for `.host` and again for `.path` in each branch), and `discourse_host.split('.')` is also recomputed repeatedly. That is a concrete per-serialization inefficiency in a likely hot path. However, the claim that a later parse “isn't covered by the earlier rescue” isn’t supported by the diff: if the first `URI(...)` call raises, `website_host` becomes nil and the method returns early, so the later `URI(...)` calls are never reached; if it doesn’t raise once, it should not raise on the same input later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed/invalid website URL inputs (e.g. 'not a url', 'javascript:alert(1)', '/path') are untested; the second URI(website.to_s).path call on line ~143 is not inside the rescue, so website_host can be nil while include_website_name is still true, emitting website_name: nil unasserted

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `include_website_name` is `website.present?`, but `website_name` can legitimately return `nil` for non-HTTP/relative/invalid inputs because `website_host` may be `nil` (e.g. `URI('/path').host` => nil) and the method early-returns. That means the serializer may emit `website_name: null` whenever `website` is non-empty but unparsable/hostless, and the added specs only cover valid `http://example.com/user` cases. However, the claim that the later `URI(website.to_s).path` call can run while `website_host` is nil is not supported, because there is an explicit `return if website_host.nil?` before those calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Second URI() call on line 143/146 without rescue: a value that parses for .host but raises on the second parse, or path edge cases (empty path, trailing slash, 'http://example.com?x=1'), are unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, every later `URI(website.to_s)` call is on the same exact string as the first parse. If the first `URI(...)` raised, `website_host` becomes `nil` and the method returns early (`return if website_host.nil?`), so the unrescued calls are never reached. If the first parse succeeded, a second parse on the same input will not suddenly raise. The rest of the finding (“path edge cases … are unverified”) is not a concrete, diff-verifiable defect; it’s speculative test coverage critique rather than a demonstrated bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the sibling-subdomain elsif branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com), including its negative case (www.other.com vs forum.example.com) and off-by-one/subdomain logic risks

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` with three paths (`if website_host == discourse_host`, an `elsif` comparing dot-segment lengths when both hosts have >2 parts, and an `else`). The added specs cover the `if` case (same host) and the `else` case (instance is a subdomain of the website host, e.g. `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). There is no test exercising the `elsif` “sibling-subdomain” branch (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) nor a negative case where the sibling comparison should fail, so the finding about missing coverage for that branch is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserting website_name equals just the host (no path appended) for a length-matching but different domain, nor for empty/trailing-slash paths, nor for query strings being silently dropped by URI#path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial `website_name` logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that conditionally appends `URI(...).path` (and never includes query/fragment). The spec only covers three cases (different domain -> host only; same domain -> host+path; parent domain -> host+path) using a single input `http://example.com/user`. It does not cover the specific branch where the instance domain has the same number of labels but a different base domain (the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && ...` path returning just `website_host`), nor cases like empty path/trailing slash, nor query strings being omitted due to using `URI#path`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend removal of websiteName computed property and switch to model.website_name in templates has zero JS/qunit test coverage; other references to websiteName would silently render empty

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `websiteName` computed property in `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates the shown template to use `model.website_name`, but it does not show any remaining references to `websiteName` that would now render empty. The claim that "other references" exist and would silently break cannot be verified from this PR diff alone. Also, while no JS/qunit tests are added, the new behavior is covered by added Ruby serializer specs, so calling it out as a concrete review issue is not diff-grounded beyond a generic "no frontend tests" statement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname with Mocha legacy stubs, coupling tests to the mock; if the implementation caches the hostname at boot the tests still pass while production differs, and there's no integration test that the serializer includes website_name via a real controller response

adjudication.rationale: In the added serializer spec, the new `website_name` behavior is verified by stubbing `Discourse.current_hostname` (`Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns(...)`). That directly couples the tests to the mocked hostname rather than exercising the real environment/stack, so the tests may not catch issues in how `current_hostname` is actually computed/used outside the unit spec. The claim about hostname caching and the absence of any integration/controller-level test can’t be fully verified from this diff alone, but the mocked dependency concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts website_name is absent from the JSON when the user has no website; the include_website_name inclusion gate is completely untested, a classic silent-failure point

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `website_name` plus an inclusion gate `include_website_name` in `user_serializer.rb` (`def include_website_name; website.present?; end`). The spec only exercises the “with filled out website” context and asserts `json[:website_name]` values there; it does not add/contain a test case for a user with no website ensuring `website_name` is omitted/nil in the JSON. That leaves the new inclusion logic untested, which is a concrete coverage gap for newly introduced behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of `websiteName` computed property from user.js.es6 may break other consumers (mobile templates, user card, plugins/themes) that still reference `websiteName`, causing silent empty rendering; no grep performed to verify remaining references

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates the shown template (`user/user.hbs`) to use `model.website_name` instead. Nothing in the provided diff indicates any remaining references to `websiteName` (e.g., in mobile templates, user card, plugins/themes), so the claim that other consumers will break cannot be verified from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Serializer builds display path via `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, dropping query strings and fragments, e.g. `http://example.com/search?q=1234` displays as `example.com/search`

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the displayed string is constructed with `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several branches, and `URI(...).path` does not include query parameters or fragments. So a URL like `http://example.com/search?q=1234#x` would display as `example.com/search` while the actual link (`href={{model.website}}` in the template) still preserves the full URL. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/behavioral choice affecting display text, not a functional correctness defect in navigation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare `http://example.com/` displays inconsistently as `example.com/` with trailing slash versus `example.com` for scheme-less input

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves `websiteName` computation to `UserSerializer#website_name` using `URI(website.to_s).host`. For scheme-less input like `example.com`, `URI(...).host` is nil, so `website_name` returns nil and the template `{{#if model.website_name}}` won’t display anything—not `example.com`. While `http://example.com/` could include a trailing `/` only in the branches that append `URI(...).path`, the stated comparison to scheme-less input (“displays as example.com”) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `rescue nil` in `website_name` swallows unparseable website values: `include_website_name` is true when `website.present?` but `website_name` returns nil for values URI() can't parse (e.g. `example.com/user`), causing a present website to silently disappear from the profile; the guard should test the parsed host instead of `website.present?`

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer`, `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, but `website_name` computes `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and immediately `return if website_host.nil?`. For website strings that are present but lack a parseable host (e.g. missing scheme like `example.com/user`), `website_name` becomes nil. The template was changed to render the website block only when `model.website_name` is present (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present `website` can silently stop displaying on the profile due to the nil `website_name`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Equal-length subdomain heuristic shows full path for unrelated sibling subdomains (e.g. `secret.example.com/private/admin` on host `forum.example.com`), causing inconsistent path-disclosure exposure across users on the same registrable domain

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branch for equal-length subdomains (`elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`) treats any sibling subdomain sharing everything after the first label as equivalent (e.g., `secret.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) and returns `website_host + URI(...).path`. This will include the full path for unrelated sibling subdomains on the same parent domain, whereas other domains only expose the host, creating the path-disclosure behavior described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for the negative case of website-is-subdomain-of-instance (e.g. `sub.example.com` vs `forums.example.com` showing host-only) and for website-present-but-unparseable case, leaving fragile else-branches untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (same host, equal-depth subdomains, and the `ends_with?` parent-domain case), and the new spec only covers: different domain (`discourse.org`), same domain (`example.com`), and website being parent of instance (`forums.example.com`). There is no test covering the opposite relationship (website is a subdomain of the instance, e.g. `sub.example.com` vs `forums.example.com`), which exercises the final `else` branch’s `... ? ... : website_host` outcome. Also, `website_name` rescues URI parse failures to `nil`, while `include_website_name` is based on `website.present?`, so a present-but-unparseable website would include `website_name` but return `nil`; that edge path is untested. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a demonstrated defect.
